newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian PM says much truth in Kulikov charges.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM says much truth in Kulikov charges.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Thursday some accusations against security tsar Alexander Lebed of planning to seize power were justified, Interfax news agency reported.

Referring to the allegations by Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov, Chernomyrdin told a meeting of security officials: "I do not conceal my concern over the fact that a considerable part of what Minister Kulikov said corresponds with reality."
But Chernomyrdin, who had summoned the defence and interior ministers and other security chiefs to discuss the accusations, said he was "far from thinking about mutinies and putsches".
Kulikov said on Wednesday that Lebed had been plotting a "creeping coup" while President Boris Yeltsin prepared for heart surgery. Lebed has denied the accusations.
"This conflict must be settled peacefully at the negotiating table," Interfax quoted Chernomyrdin as saying.
